t: 3587 — Minimum Adjacent Swaps to Alternate Parity
o: Only parities matter, not values. A valid arrangement is one of two parity patterns: starting even or starting odd. Since |#even − #odd| must be at most 1 for any alternation to exist, return -1 otherwise. For a feasible pattern, each misplaced element pairs with another misplaced element and one adjacent swap fixes both, so the cost is (number of mismatches)/2. Try whichever pattern(s) match the multiset of parities and take the cheaper.
k: Feasibility depends only on counts: |even − odd| ≤ 1, else -1.
Adjacent swaps exchange parities pairwise, so cost = mismatches / 2 for a matched target pattern.
A pattern is usable only if its slot counts exactly equal the counts of even/odd elements.

a.i: Compare the array's parity sequence against the two alternating templates. A template is achievable only when the number of even slots in it equals the actual number of even elements. For an achievable template, count mismatched positions; each adjacent swap resolves exactly two mismatches, giving the minimal swap count by a standard inversion/exchange argument.
s: For template starting with even (usable iff evens == ceil(n/2)), count positions where parity differs; answer candidate = mismatches // 2.
Same for the odd-start template (usable iff odds == ceil(n/2)).
a.t: O(n) — one counting pass plus up to two linear scans

w: The key correctness fact: with distinct elements, moving parities into a fixed pattern via adjacent swaps costs exactly half the mismatches (each swap places two elements correctly; a potential-function argument shows you cannot do better). Pitfalls: forgetting the -1 case, allowing a template whose slot counts don't match, and parity bugs with negative numbers in JS/Java (values here are positive, but be careful in general).
